title: Work out which commits a rebase replays
acceptanceCriteria: A commit upstream can reach through **any** parent — including a merge commit's second parent — is not replayed
The commits come back oldest first, the order of the `pick` lines
A commit whose `patch` upstream already has (a cherry-pick, or a one-commit squash merge) is skipped
Only commits upstream gained since the two sides split count as "already upstream": re-applying a change from the shared history is still replayed
After a multi-commit squash merge, the old base's commits are replayed again
With the old base as upstream (`rebase --onto main feature-a`), only the branch's own commit is replayed
